en: Besides subagents, one other key feature
that can make Claude Code better
are agent skills,
which is actually an open standard supported
by other AI coding tools like Cursor,
OpenCode, and many others as well.
The idea behind agent skills is that you
define
extra dynamically loaded pieces of context
that can come in helpful for certain tasks.
For example, a document or a combination of
documents that describes some best practices
on building React components or
Python classes or C++ classes or whatever
applies to your project. And a skill
is simply the combination of a skill.md file
that is always required and we'll create one
together in a second.
And then some optional additional documents
or folders with documents inside. Skills can
even contain get access to scripts which may
be executed by the AI. So if you, for
example, want to define a cleanup script
that deletes files in a certain way, you can
do so using Python or JavaScript.
But in my experience, the most useful skills
for building applications are simply
knowledge skills that provide extra
information, extra instructions, extra best
practices, and so on.
But if you need to include scripts or extra
assets like images with diagrams, you can do
so as well. But let's now build such a
skill.
